subject: Film & Cinema
title: Practical Effects: Real Magic
description: A micro-lesson that makes Practical Effects: Real Magic usable.

hook.text: They actually flipped a real truck in The Dark Knight. No CGI. That's why it looks perfect.

buildup.text: Practical effects use real objects — miniatures, prosthetics, pyrotechnics — captured on camera.

discovery.text: Mad Max: Fury Road built real vehicles and did real stunts in the desert for maximum impact.

twist.text: Practical effects are expensive and dangerous. Studios increasingly prefer cheaper CGI alternatives.

climax.text: Audiences can instinctively feel the difference between real and digital — weight, texture, danger.

punchline.text: Real things on screen feel real. Always.

quiz.question: Why did Mad Max: Fury Road use mostly practical effects?
options: Real stunts and vehicles create visceral impact audiences can feel
